newsitem.title: UK: Kwik Save shares gain after results.
newsitem.headline: Kwik Save shares gain after results.

text.p: Shares in Kwik Save Plc rose in early trading on Thursday after the supermarket operator's full-year results beat expectations and the company launched a new recovery programme.
The stock was up 6p at 310 by 0812 GMT in thin trade of 5,000 shares.
Analysts said the results were poor but were not as bad as some had expected. They also said the company still faces significant challenges with its "New Generation Kwik Save" programme.
"The results were very bad but were not as bad as they could have been," said Bill Myers, analyst at Williams de Broe. "But the pain they are going to have to take is quite horrendous."
Kwik Save posted a 28 percent drop in pre-tax profit before exceptionals to 90.3 million stg, compared with analyst expectations mostly in a range between 82.0 million stg and 90.0 million.

Chief executive Graeme Bowler said the company's new generation programme signalled "a major cultural change in the comapny designed to ensure that we have people, systems and skills responsive and flexible enough to compete effectively whatever tomorrow's trading conditions may bring."
